Com `async: true`, os envios para ESTE d: With `async: true`, sends to THIS recipient go out one at a time, in the order the API received them. Sends to other recipients still run in parallel. This order is the order of arrival at the backend: requests fired in parallel by the client have no order to preserve — send them serially. There is a limit on accumulated pending sends per recipient; when it is exceeded the API responds 429 and the client should retry later. Ignored without `async: true` and in Official API sessions (`cloud_api`), where sending is always synchronous.

Returns the Meta access token stored for a cloud_api connection, DECRYPTED, along with the token type. The `id` accepts the connection id or the session id (`cloud-<uuid>`).

`data.accessToken` is the raw Graph token — treat it as a secret (it sends messages and manages the WABA). `data.kind` is `permanent` (never expires, e.g. System User), `long_lived` (~60-day token from Embedded Signup), `short_lived` (~1h token from the code exchange) or `unknown` (Meta's /debug_token could not be queried). `data.expiresAt` (ISO-8601, null when permanent), `data.expiresInDays`, `data.isValid`, `data.scopes`, `data.type` (Meta's own USER/SYSTEM_USER label) and `data.label` (summary in pt-BR) describe the token.
